sentence: This project uses functional near-infrared spectroscopy and deep learning to find what drives relapse in people with opioid use disorder.
This project builds a tool that uses wastewater to detect and forecast infectious viral diseases early.
This project offers a two-week course on quantitative light microscopy and computational analysis of biological images.
This project collects and provides human tissue and blood samples from cancer patients to support cancer research.
This project studies factors that liver cancer cells need to function, called transcriptional master regulators, as possible treatment targets.
This project studies how the brain's response to odor is changed by obesity and how that affects neuroendocrine function.
This project studies why children with autism spectrum disorder also develop attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, using genes, stem cells, brain imaging and behavior.
This project studies lung cells called pulmonary ionocytes, how they develop and function, and how they interact with other cells in the airways.
This project tests a radiopharmaceutical therapy that uses antibodies to deliver alpha- or beta-emitting radionuclides to lung cancer tumors.
This project compares risk factors and tumor genomics in breast cancer among Black women and White women to find what drives differences in the disease.
This project uses whole-genome sequence information to study why people differ in their risk of coronary artery disease.
This project builds computational tools for processing RNA sequencing data from improved technologies.
This project provides a fluorescence microscope that shows protein complexes inside cells at the nanometer scale.
This project builds instruments and computer tools for studying protein and nucleoprotein complexes using native mass spectrometry.
This project tries to find out how enhancer-regulating epigenetic modifiers work in pluripotent stem cells.
This project studies a complex in kidney cells that cannot regenerate after sudden damage, aiming to halt progression to chronic kidney disease.
This project tests whether a therapy aimed at differentiated cells can prevent relapse of rhabdomyosarcoma, a childhood muscle cancer.
This project studies spreading depolarization waves and brain swelling that injure brain cells after neurologic emergencies such as stroke and head trauma.
